steps.text: Fifty-eight hours into the operation...

steps.name: W Squad Member
steps.text: *Sarkaz swearing*! How are we supposed to fight these guys when our equipment doesn't even come close to theirs?

steps.name: W Squad Member
steps.text: Evacuate! Now!

steps.name: Sarkaz Royal Court Soldier A
steps.text: Lifebone's signal is strong. We have a good fix on its location.

steps.name: Sarkaz Royal Court Soldier A
steps.text: Forward! Scout casters advance!

steps.name: Sarkaz Royal Court Soldier A
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Sarkaz Royal Court Soldier B
steps.text: Look out! Enemies!

steps.name: Sarkaz Royal Court Commander
steps.text: In formation! Watch for ambush!

steps.name: Sarkaz Royal Court Commander
steps.text: Infantry, form a line! Casters, provide cover!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Royal Court elites, under Manfred's direct command... a lot of them.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: No heavy firepower, though. I can at least slow them down.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hoederer was right...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ulšulah knows our defenses are weak, and she'll tell Manfred. We can use this to our advantage.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The Military Commission won't allow Lifebone to fall into enemy hands. Manfred would destroy it if he had no other choice.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Draw them in. Avoid direct confrontation.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Manfred will be cautious about the use of heavy weapons as long as he thinks there's a chance to retake the skeleton intact. That gives us a chance to buy time.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: With enough time, there's a sliver of hope.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This had better work, Hoederer.
What's this bothersome shadow?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Nachzehrer Arts—

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Mercenaries are just mercenaries. Maybe you could hold your own in a one-to-one fight, or small-scale confrontations.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: But where did you find the nerve to fight a real war?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: I've always been curious. What made mercenaries like you choose to become enemies of the Military Commission?
The shadow blends into the vast darkness, yet not enough to escape the decay that closely follows.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: We have intel of a merc who could manipulate shadows. Are you Ines?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: An outsider, dressing herself up as Sarkaz, participating in the wars of the Sarkaz... what are you? A Sarkaz fangirl?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I become less interested when the Sarkaz talk too much—
Shadows erupt from beneath the Nachzehrer, morphing into sharp blades that streak towards her chest, only to tear through layers of tattered cloth.
The Nachzehrer's ribbons are wrapped tightly around the shadow blades, until they shatter and disintegrate. The Nachzehrer's knife presses against Ines's throat.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Nice party trick, not enough to take down a real soldier, though. Amateur.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Consider yourself lucky that I don't approve of the Sanguinarch's methods.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: A new era for the Sarkaz is dawning. Mercenaries like you who strayed from the path should get a second chance.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Are you the leader of this rabble? I am Lieutenant General Nadine, General Manfred's deputy, and I offer you the chance to surrender. I suggest you take it.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: You don't look scared.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Scared of what? A wet-behind-the-ear rookie who's on a real battlefield for the first time?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I know your type. You got into the Military Commission's academy because of your Royal Court bloodline, studied a few theories, and got promoted to staff officer as soon as you graduated.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Sorry to say but real war is a bit harder than those exams you passed.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: You'll pay the price for your futile taunting.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's not futile if it distracts you.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Who's the amateur now, Lieutenant General?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Damn, this thing packs a punch. That heap of deadwood wasn't lying.

steps.name: W
steps.text: How did you know I was coming?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I could smell the explosives from a mile away.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Oh yeah? Guess we're starting to build chemistry.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I'd rather not have my brain cells mixed with your bomb-blasted ones, thank you very much.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Enough small talk. How many did the Military Commission send? I'll blow them all the way back to Kazdel.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Where did you go? And what's with the outfit change?

steps.name: W
steps.text: My old garb was a little frayed, so I had to improvise.

steps.name: W
steps.text: You'd never believe what I ran into out there.

steps.name: W
steps.text: *cough*... You're tough for a heap of deadwood.

steps.name: W
steps.text: If I can't blow you up, at least I'll blast all this stuff.

steps.name: Qalid'čoa
steps.text: These weapons and armor are relics of great Sarkaz heroes.

steps.name: Qalid'čoa
steps.text: Your weapons will not harm them.

steps.name: W
steps.text: So you're saying these things are blast proof?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Alright, don't mind if I do!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Better for them to get some sunshine with me than rot in here.

steps.name: Qalid'čoa
steps.text: Young mercenary, you should respect the Sarkaz heroes—

steps.name: W
steps.text: What's going on? Where's Manfred? I could use a target to try out my new gear.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Don't be hasty. You'll ruin our plan if you make too much of a scene.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Why? Does Hoederer have some trick up his sleeve again?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: You have squandered your only chance to live.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: You refused to join the Military Commission. Now, you will fuel the war.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I hear the sound of fighting.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Things are going smoothly, sir. We haven't run into much resistance.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: The mercenaries are no match for us, but it would be difficult to stop them from destroying Lifebone out of desperation.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No, they won't do it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: This book has no ending.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: It's just a manuscript from an unknown writer. Hardly worthy of your attention, general.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I remember you, veteran.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You like reading? Not just any book, but the kind that promotes this sort of... pessimism towards war.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No need to justify your reading interests.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Be honest with me, mercenary. What ending would you write, if you were the author?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...The hero returns home.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Not a death in battle?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: A warrior should think of more than his home, in battle.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Whose homes should he think of, then?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Your empathy is admirable.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Pardon my impudence.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Sentimentality is a necessary trait in an author.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: But indecision is the worst trait in a soldier.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...I understand.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Your compassion is the reason I've kept you alive for so long.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: But you should have gone back to Kazdel, become a teacher or a farmer, giving up your ludicrous mercenary career.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Lifebone was meant to be a way home for all warriors.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Remain vigilant. A beast is most dangerous when cornered.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Keep up the pressure. Give them no quarter.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: Sir! Look out!
No one sees the smoke coagulate into a blade, as subtly as mist condenses into dew.
The soldier beside Manfred throws himself in front of his commander. The blade impales him, delaying it for an instant.
Enough for Manfred to draw his sword.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You won't—
It all happens in the blink of an eye. Arts coagulate by Manfred's side, just as he swings his sword upwards.
But Ascalon's blade is swifter. This time, there is no doubt, no hesitation.
A blow long due.
The assassin and the general cross blades, severing life and death.
And all of their past ties.

steps.name: Royal Court Soldier
steps.text: General!
The sword impales Ascalon's shoulder.
But the sleeve-blade pierces Manfred's heart.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You've... lived up to your words...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: As I said I would.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If you had made up your mind... I would have died at your hand... a long time ago.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I still have regrets about not killing you the night you left Kazdel.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...Farewell.

steps.name: Manfred?
steps.text: What a shame. I thought you would at least shed a tear.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Wha—

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: You would have recognized us under any other circumstances.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Quick and direct, weren't you?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Did you care too much about him, or too little?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Everything went exactly as Manfred expected.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: You still don't know Manfred well enough, for all the years that you've been rivals.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: But he knows you all too well.

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: We've engaged the Royal Court on both the north and south sides, and we're pulling back our lines as planned.

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: Everything has gone according to plan, so far.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Good...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Any sign of Manfred?

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: Not yet...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: He wouldn't be content to just sit in the back and bark orders at a time like this.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...I hope things go smoothly for Ascalon.

steps.name: Mercenary Scout
steps.text: No, she won't be coming back.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Wha—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I knew you would be here.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Manfred...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Delay tactics... did you really think protecting this skeleton would help you turn the tables?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I gave you a chance. I gave you far too many chances. You knew the smart thing to do!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Once again, you're having Sarkaz slaughter Sarkaz.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Haven't you had enough of 'wars' like this?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You disappoint me...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Their death is not on me, but your naivete!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You should have left a long time ago. Isn't this what you had always longed for?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Now, your mercenaries will die here, as will my soldiers, for something so meaningless... have you not learned the lessons of the civil war?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: That's why the Sarkaz shouldn't repeat the mistakes of the past! Haven't we all seen what the civil war became?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We lost an entire generation to the civil war, and you're trying to kill more?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Nothing will come of this war. This war against all of Terra!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Something will come of it. Something must.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You have seen it already. You just refuse to acknowledge it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: To hate and be hated... if that's the Military Commission's goal, then mission accomplished.

spans.text: To hate and be hated... if that's the Military Commission's goal, then

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Don't you understand? That's the reason I needed you to get out of this!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Yes, the civil war cost Kazdel an entire generation, and made you and I out of the survivors... Murderers who can only live by the sword.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Why have you stayed, if you wanted to change all of this?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: There was so much more you could have done and should have done.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: So what if I returned to Kazdel? What happens next?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: How do I describe to the children the fields where their fathers, their mothers, their brothers, and their sisters are buried? How do I make them believe in another future?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Hatred is a means to unity, but you cannot let that unity become the spark for a new hatred.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I can't leave. Not while the war continues.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: So you have chosen to live and die with the war.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: In that case, I will give you the answer.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ngh—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Hoederer, you coward.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You lack even the courage to keep living.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: This is what makes you so contemptible.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: ...This is what disappoints me so deeply.
